label: Open bugs
means: Problems that were reported and are not fixed yet; fewer is better.
goal_source: template goal: no known bug left open
source: state: gh api graphql: repository.issues, open issues of the Bug type (params.bug_type; on a user's repo, which has no types, the label params.bug_label), by area label (params.area_labels)

label: Parked issues
means: Open issues over a day old that are not a bug or a quick fix; such work waits on the board. Fewer is better.
goal_source: GitHub docs, Managing issue types in an organization (read 2026-11-10): a type says what kind of work an issue is; GitHub docs, Adding items to your project (read 2026-11-10): a draft issue captures an idea on the board; template goal: none parked
source: state: gh api graphql: repository.issues, open issues older than params.park_hours whose issueType is not in params.issue_types; not measured for a user's repo, which has no issue types

label: Issues with an area label
means: Share of issues tagged with the part of the project they affect; higher is better.
goal_source: template goal: every issue names its area, so it reaches whoever owns that area
source: state: gh api graphql: repository.issues, labels named in params.area_labels

label: Unused labels
means: Labels in the picker that no issue or pull request carries and no setting names; fewer is better.
goal_source: GitHub docs, Managing labels (read 2026-11-10), and GitHub changelog, Label archiving is generally available (2026-08-27): an archived label leaves the picker and keeps its history; template goal: none unused
source: state: gh api repos/{repo}/labels (archived_at) and gh api graphql: repository.labels (issues and pullRequests totalCount); a label not archived that nothing carries and that is neither params.bug_label nor in params.area_labels

label: Issue forms in order
means: Share of intake checks that hold: each issue form parses, each sets a type, blank issues are off. Higher is better.
goal_source: GitHub docs, Syntax for issue forms and Configuring issue templates for your repository (read 2026-11-10): a form needs a name, a description and a body, may set its issue type, and config.yml turns blank issues off; template goal: every check holds
source: state: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE: each YAML issue form parsed for the keys GitHub requires (name, description, body) and its type, and config.yml for blank_issues_enabled; a form that does not parse is a miss, as GitHub rejects it; the type check is against params.issue_types and is left out when that is empty

label: Bugs closed by a merged PR
means: Share of recently fixed bugs that an accepted code change closed, not a close by hand; higher is better.
goal_source: GitHub docs, Linking a pull request to an issue: a merged pull request with a closing keyword closes its issue; template goal: every fixed bug closes that way
source: gh api graphql: repository.issues, the last 20 issues of the Bug type (params.bug_type; on a user's repo, the label params.bug_label) closed as completed (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median, few enough that new closes replace them), ClosedEvent closer (a merged PR, or a commit from one); left out before the 20 are taken: not-planned and duplicate closes, and a record, closed by hand within params.record_minutes of opening

label: Issues reopened
means: Share of recently closed reports that had been reopened because a fix did not hold; lower is better.
goal_source: template goal: one fix in twenty fails to hold at most
source: gh api graphql: repository.issues, the last 20 issues closed as completed (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median, few enough that new closes replace them), REOPENED_EVENT count; not-planned and duplicate closes, and a record closed by hand within params.record_minutes of opening, left out

label: Latest issue's hours to close
means: How long the most recently fixed issue took from filed to closed, in hours; lower is better.
goal_source: template goal (2026-11-03): an issue closes within a day of being filed
source: latest: gh api graphql: repository.issues, the latest issue closed as completed (a point in time, never a median over a window): closedAt minus createdAt; a not-planned or duplicate close, or a record closed by hand within params.record_minutes of opening, is left out

label: Oldest open issue
means: How long the longest-waiting open issue has been open, in days; lower is better.
goal_source: template goal: no issue waits more than two days
source: state: gh api graphql: repository.issues, open issues, age at read time

label: Prose words, the latest card
means: Words the latest issue spends outside tables, diagrams and code; fewer is better, so the visuals carry it.
goal_source: template goal: a card reads in under 20 seconds; adults read non-fiction at about 238 words a minute (Brysbaert, How many words do we read per minute?, Journal of Memory and Language, 2019), so 75 words take about 19 seconds
source: latest: gh api graphql: of the 20 newest issues (N = 20, a template choice: few enough that new issues replace them), the latest with a body; words left after removing tables, fenced code and diagrams, inline code, link targets, HTML comments and params.pr_body_ignore (proseWords in github.mjs)

label: Cards with a visual
means: Share of issues that show their facts in a table, a diagram, a chart or an image; higher is better.
goal_source: template goal: every card shows its facts visually; GitHub draws tables, Mermaid diagrams and charts, maps and images in issues (GitHub docs, Creating diagrams)
source: gh api graphql: the body of each of the 20 newest issues (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median, few enough that new issues replace them); a table, a Mermaid, GeoJSON, TopoJSON or STL block, or an image outside code (hasVisual in github.mjs)

label: Merged PRs green at head
means: Share of accepted code changes whose automatic checks all passed at the end; higher is better.
goal_source: GitHub docs, About protected branches: Require status checks before merging; template goal: every check passes at the merged head
source: gh api graphql: the last 20 merged pullRequests (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median, few enough that new merges replace them), head commit statusCheckRollup: state SUCCESS, or each check's latest run passed, since the rollup also counts an earlier run of a check that ran again on the same commit

label: Merged PRs reviewed at head
means: Share of accepted code changes that a person reviewed at the exact commit that was accepted; higher is better.
goal_source: GitHub docs, About protected branches: Require pull request reviews before merging, and Dismiss stale pull request approvals when new commits are pushed, so a review covers the commit that merges
source: gh api graphql: the last 20 merged pullRequests (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median, few enough that new merges replace them); reviewed when a person submitted a review whose commit.oid is the merged headRefOid, or a member posted a comment whose first line is Review: MERGE at that SHA, no later than mergedAt (bot reviews left out)

label: Fixed after the first review
means: Share of reviewed changes that needed another commit after their first review; lower means more pass first time.
goal_source: template goal: three in four reviewed changes pass their first review
source: gh api graphql: the last 20 merged pullRequests (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median, few enough that new merges replace them) with a person's review, or a member's Review: MERGE|BLOCK at <sha> comment, before the merge; fixed when that first one read a commit other than the merged head, as a BLOCK at an earlier head does

label: Reverts in the last 20 merges
means: Recent accepted changes that undo an earlier one, because something broke; fewer is better.
goal_source: DORA, Accelerate State of DevOps Report 2023: elite teams' change failure rate is 5% and high performers' 10%, which is 1 and 2 of the last 20 merges
source: gh api graphql: the last 20 merged pullRequests (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median, few enough that new merges replace them); a PR titled Revert "<title>" undoes the merged PR with that title, and every such revert among the 20 counts

label: Branch commits through a PR
means: Share of recent commits on the default branch that came through a pull request, not pushed in; higher is better.
goal_source: GitHub docs, About protected branches: Require a pull request before merging
source: gh api graphql: the last 20 commits on the default branch (N = 20, as for merged PRs: each merge adds at least one commit), associatedPullRequests merged

label: Merged outside the default branch
means: Recent accepted changes merged into a side branch, where the default branch's rules may not apply; fewer is better.
goal_source: GitHub docs, About stacked pull requests (read 2026-11-10): a stack's merge requirements come from the bottom pull request's base branch, and outside a stack rules and checks often only trigger for the bottom pull request; template goal: every change merges into the default branch, a large one as a stack
source: gh api graphql: the last 20 merged pullRequests (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median, few enough that new merges replace them), baseRefName other than its base repository's defaultBranchRef.name, read in the same query; each with its reviewed lines

label: Prose words, the latest PR description
means: Words the latest accepted change's description spends outside tables, code and diagrams; fewer is better.
goal_source: template goal: a description reads in under a minute; adults read non-fiction at about 238 words a minute (Brysbaert, How many words do we read per minute?, Journal of Memory and Language, 2019), so 150 words take about 40 seconds and 300 about 75
source: latest: gh api graphql: of the last 20 merged pullRequests (N = 20, a template choice: few enough that new merges replace them), the latest with a description; words left after removing tables, fenced code and diagrams, inline code, link targets, HTML comments and params.pr_body_ignore (proseWords in github.mjs)

label: PR descriptions with a table
means: Share of accepted changes whose description shows its facts in a table.
goal_source: template goal: every description shows its facts in a table, which a reviewer scans faster than prose
source: gh api graphql: the body of each of the last 20 merged pullRequests (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median, few enough that new merges replace them); a markdown table row followed by its separator row, outside fenced blocks (hasTable in github.mjs)

label: PRs linking an issue
means: Share of accepted changes whose description links the issue it fixes or serves; higher is better.
goal_source: GitHub docs, Linking a pull request to an issue (read 2026-11-04): close, fix or resolve before an issue reference closes it on merge; template goal: every change names its issue, with Part of #N when it only serves one
source: gh api graphql: the body of each of the last 20 merged pullRequests (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median, few enough that new merges replace them); a closing keyword (close, fix or resolve) or Part of before an issue reference, outside fenced blocks (linksIssue in github.mjs)

label: Lines changed, the latest PR
means: Lines the latest accepted change asks a reviewer to read, less lockfiles, snapshots and moved lines; lower is better.
goal_source: SmartBear's code review study at Cisco: a reviewer should take in no more than 200 to 400 lines at a time (SmartBear, Best Kept Secrets of Peer Code Review, 2006)
source: latest: gh api graphql: the latest merged pullRequest, additions plus deletions, less the lines of lockfiles, generated code, data snapshots and params.not_reviewed (NOT_REVIEWED in github.mjs), and two for each line its merge commit moves (git diff, readLines in github-reviews.mjs)

label: Share over 400 lines
means: Share of accepted changes too big to review in one sitting; lower is better.
goal_source: SmartBear's code review study at Cisco: a reviewer should take in no more than 200 to 400 lines at a time (SmartBear, Best Kept Secrets of Peer Code Review, 2006); the 10% share is a template goal
source: gh api graphql: the last 20 merged pullRequests (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median, few enough that new merges replace them), additions plus deletions, less lockfile, generated and snapshot lines and the lines each merge commit moves (git diff, readLines in github-reviews.mjs)

label: Latest PR's hours to merge
means: How long the most recently merged pull request took from opened to merged, in hours, by stage; lower is better.
goal_source: DORA, Accelerate State of DevOps Report 2023: elite teams' lead time for changes is under a day and high performers' under a week; merging is part of that lead time
source: latest: gh api graphql: the latest merged pullRequest (a point in time, never a median over a window): mergedAt minus createdAt; its stages from head check times and reviews at head

label: Minutes from all green to merge
means: Minutes a merged PR waited from all checks green at its head to merge, median of the last 10; lower is better.
goal_source: template goal, no public benchmark: review and merge within an hour of green CI
source: gh api graphql: the last 10 merged pullRequests (N = 10, a template choice), median of mergedAt minus the last check's completion on the merged head, for each PR whose head rollup is SUCCESS

label: Open PRs now
means: Code changes waiting right now to be checked and accepted, by how long each has waited; fewer is better.
goal_source: template goal: a queue short enough to review in one sitting
source: state: gh api graphql: open pullRequests, by age at read time

label: Longest wait after all green
means: Minutes the longest-waiting open change has sat since its checks passed, unreviewed or unmerged; lower is better.
goal_source: template goal, no public benchmark: review and merge within an hour of green CI, as for pull_requests.green_to_merge_minutes
source: state: gh api graphql: open pullRequests that are not drafts, not Dependabot's, green at head (statusCheckRollup SUCCESS) and not blocked there (a Review: BLOCK verdict, or reviewDecision CHANGES_REQUESTED); the longest time since the head's last check completed, at read time, the five longest as rows

label: Open PRs with a conflict
means: Waiting changes that clash with the latest default branch and must be fixed before they can merge; fewer is better.
goal_source: template goal: no waiting change needs a rebase
source: state: gh api graphql: open pullRequests, mergeable is CONFLICTING

label: Oldest open PR
means: How long the longest-waiting code change has sat open and undecided, in days; lower is better.
goal_source: template goal: no change waits more than a week
source: state: gh api graphql: open pullRequests, age at read time

label: Open Dependabot PRs
means: Automatic proposals to update our libraries that nobody has accepted yet; fewer is better.
goal_source: template goal: dependency updates merge as they arrive
source: state: gh api graphql: open pullRequests authored by dependabot, by ecosystem label

label: Actions pinned to a SHA
means: Share of outside tools in our automatic jobs locked to one exact version; higher is better.
goal_source: GitHub docs, Security hardening for GitHub Actions: pinning an action to a full-length commit SHA is the only way to use it as an immutable release; Workflow dependency lockfiles (read 2026-11-10): a locked reference runs its recorded commit; OpenSSF Scorecard, Pinned-Dependencies
source: state: .github/workflows/*.yml: each job's and step's uses:, read from the parsed YAML, ending in a 40-character SHA, or a step's reference that .github/workflows/actions.lock records for its workflow; local ./ and $/ actions left out

label: Workflows with explicit permissions
means: Share of automatic job files that spell out what they are allowed to do; higher is better.
goal_source: GitHub docs, Automatic token authentication: grant GITHUB_TOKEN the least access each workflow needs, with a permissions key; OpenSSF Scorecard, Token-Permissions
source: state: .github/workflows/*.yml: a top-level permissions: block, or one on every job

label: Workflows locked to recorded commits
means: Share of workflows that call outside actions and are in the lockfile, so each run uses the commits recorded there.
goal_source: GitHub docs, Secure use reference (read 2026-11-10): lock workflow dependencies with a lockfile, which supersedes SHA pinning where adopted; Workflow dependency lockfiles (read 2026-11-10): every dependency of an onboarded workflow must be in the lockfile, and its recorded commit is what runs
source: state: each .github/workflows/*.yml with an outside action in a step, against the workflows listed in .github/workflows/actions.lock; a workflow with only a job-level call or local actions is left out, since a lockfile does not cover them

label: In progress, no open PR
means: Cards in the in-progress column that no open pull request is building: stalled or waiting; lower is better.
goal_source: DORA, Work in process limits (read 2026-11-10): the point of a limit is to expose problems in the system so they can be addressed; template goal: one session builds one card, so a count of cards limits nothing, a card in progress has an open pull request, and pull_requests.open_now carries the limit on work in flight
source: state: gh api graphql: repositoryOwner projectsV2 named params.project_title (the repo name by default), items in the column before the last of params.project_columns with no linked pull request whose state is OPEN; the breakdown counts every column

label: Done cards with a merged PR
means: Share of finished board tasks that link to an accepted code change; higher is better.
goal_source: template goal: every finished card links the change that finished it
source: state: gh api graphql: projectsV2 items in the last of params.project_columns, linked pull requests, the PR itself, or a PR URL in a draft card

label: Board workflows on
means: Share of the built-in board workflows that are on: add, link, close and merge move a card unaided; higher is better.
goal_source: GitHub docs, Using the built-in automations (read 2026-11-10): a board sets Status when an item is added, closed or merged and adds matching items; template goal: all five on, the fifth moving a card to in progress when a pull request links its issue
source: state: gh api graphql: repositoryOwner projectsV2 named params.project_title, its workflows and whether each is enabled, against params.project_workflows

label: Cards read at a glance
means: Share of open cards with a picture and at most 75 words of prose, so the picture carries the card; higher is better.
goal_source: template goal: every card shows its work as a picture with few words; GitHub docs, Basic writing and formatting syntax (read 2026-11-10): an image in a body is drawn in place; Anthropic, Best practices for Claude Code (read 2026-11-10): paste the screenshot of the design, and a screenshot next to the mockup is a check; 75 words read in about 19 seconds (Brysbaert, 2019)
source: state: gh api graphql: projectsV2 draft and issue cards outside the last of params.project_columns: the body has an image, or on an issue card a Mermaid, GeoJSON, TopoJSON or STL block (a draft card shows those as code), and at most params.card_words words outside tables and code

label: Bugs and fixes on board
means: Open issue cards that are a bug or a quick fix; those are issues, not cards, so lower is better.
goal_source: template goal: a bug or a quick fix is an issue and a feature is a card; GitHub docs, Managing issue types in an organization (read 2026-11-10): a type says what kind of work an issue is; Microsoft Learn, Show bugs on backlogs and boards (read 2026-11-10) lists keeping bugs off the board as one of three options
source: state: gh api graphql: projectsV2 issue cards outside the last of params.project_columns that carry params.bug_label or a type in params.issue_types

label: Closed issues off Done
means: Closed issues whose board card is not in the last column; a merged PR should have moved it, so lower is better.
goal_source: template goal: a closed issue's card is Done; GitHub docs, Using the built-in automations (read 2026-11-11): the Item closed workflow sets Status when an issue closes; Git Crafter issue 791: a card stayed In Progress after its issue closed by a merged PR
source: state: gh api graphql: projectsV2 issue cards whose issue is CLOSED and whose Status is not the last of params.project_columns

label: Oldest card in progress
means: Days the longest-waiting card has sat in the in-progress column; lower is better.
goal_source: DORA, Working in small batches (updated 2025-12-08, read 2026-11-10): any batch of code that takes longer than a week to complete and check is too big; template goal: no card stays in progress past a week, near is two weeks
source: state: gh api graphql: projectsV2 items in the column before the last of params.project_columns: read time minus the earliest Status updatedAt

label: Latest card's hours to done
means: How long the card most recently marked done took from its first pull request opening, in hours; lower is better.
goal_source: template goal (2026-11-03): a task finishes within three days of its first pull request
source: latest: gh api graphql: projectsV2, the item most recently moved to the done column that has a linked PR: Status updatedAt minus the first linked PR's createdAt

label: Security policy
means: Whether the repo tells people how to report a vulnerability, in its own SECURITY.md or the organization's; on is better.
goal_source: GitHub docs, Adding a security policy to your repository
source: state: gh api graphql: repository.isSecurityPolicyEnabled

label: Dependabot alerts
means: Whether GitHub warns when a library the repo uses has a known vulnerability; on is better.
goal_source: GitHub docs, About Dependabot alerts
source: state: gh api graphql: repository.hasVulnerabilityAlertsEnabled

label: Code scanning
means: Whether GitHub scans the repo's own code for vulnerabilities and errors; on is better, even where it costs.
goal_source: GitHub docs, About code scanning
source: state: gh api repos/{repo}/code-scanning/default-setup (state configured) or code-scanning/analyses; off is a miss even when the plan charges for it

label: Secret scanning and push protection
means: Whether GitHub finds secrets in the repo and blocks pushes that hold one; both on is better, even where it costs.
goal_source: GitHub docs, About secret scanning, and About push protection
source: state: gh api repos/{repo}: security_and_analysis.secret_scanning and secret_scanning_push_protection both enabled; off is a miss even when the plan charges for it

label: Code quality
means: Whether GitHub checks the repo's code for maintainability and reliability problems; on is better, even where it costs.
goal_source: GitHub docs, GitHub Code Quality
source: state: gh api repos/{repo}/code-quality/setup (state configured); off is a miss even when the plan charges for it

label: Open Dependabot vulnerabilities
means: Known vulnerabilities in the libraries the repo uses that are not fixed yet, by severity; fewer is better.
goal_source: GitHub docs, About Dependabot alerts: each alert is a known vulnerability in a dependency; template goal: none left open
source: state: gh api dependabot/alerts: open alerts that are vulnerabilities (malware left out), by security_advisory.severity

label: Open malware alerts
means: Libraries the repo uses that GitHub flags as malware; none is the only safe number.
goal_source: GitHub docs, Dependabot malware alerts (read 2026-11-10): an alert means a dependency is a known malicious package; template goal: none open
source: state: gh api repos/{repo}/dependabot/alerts --paginate: open alerts whose security_advisory.classification is malware

label: Open code scanning alerts
means: Problems code scanning found in the repo's own code that are not fixed yet; not counted while it is off.
goal_source: GitHub docs, About code scanning alerts; template goal: none open
source: state: gh api repos/{repo}/code-scanning/alerts --paginate: open alerts by severity; could_not_check while code scanning is off

label: Open secret scanning alerts
means: Secrets found in the repo that are not revoked yet; not counted while secret scanning is off.
goal_source: GitHub docs, About secret scanning: a leaked secret should be revoked; template goal: none open
source: state: gh api repos/{repo}/secret-scanning/alerts --paginate: open alerts by secret type; could_not_check while secret scanning is off

label: Open code quality findings
means: Maintainability and reliability problems GitHub found in the code; not counted while code quality is off.
goal_source: template goal: none open (GitHub docs, GitHub Code Quality)
source: state: gh api repos/{repo}/code-quality/findings?state=open --paginate, by severity; could_not_check while code quality is off

label: Production security headers
means: How many standard safety settings the live site tells browsers to use; more is better.
goal_source: OWASP Secure Headers Project: send Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy
source: state: HEAD params.site_url: Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy

label: GITHUB_TOKEN reads only by default
means: Whether a workflow's token can only read unless the workflow asks for more; on is better.
goal_source: GitHub docs, Security hardening for GitHub Actions: grant the GITHUB_TOKEN the least access it needs; Managing GitHub Actions settings for a repository: Workflow permissions
source: state: gh api repos/{repo}/actions/permissions/workflow: default_workflow_permissions is read

label: Actions policy settings that are on
means: Share of two repo settings that are on: only selected actions may run, and each must be pinned to a full commit.
goal_source: GitHub docs, Governing execution of GitHub Actions workflows (read 2026-11-10): keep the full-length commit SHA requirement on beside a lockfile; Managing GitHub Actions settings for a repository: allow only selected actions and reusable workflows
source: state: gh api repos/{repo}/actions/permissions: allowed_actions is not all, and sha_pinning_required is true

label: Privileged jobs running pull request code
means: Jobs that run with the repo's secrets on a pull request's own code; none is the only safe number.
goal_source: GitHub docs, Security hardening for GitHub Actions: pull_request_target and workflow_run, used with a checkout of an untrusted pull request, expose the repo; OpenSSF Scorecard, Dangerous-Workflow
source: state: .github/workflows/*.yml: jobs of a pull_request_target or workflow_run workflow that check out the pull request's code (actions/checkout of its head, gh pr checkout, or git fetch or checkout of refs/pull/*)

label: Dependabot updates with a cooldown
means: Share of Dependabot update feeds that wait before taking a new release, so a bad one is caught first; higher is better.
goal_source: GitHub docs, Dependabot options reference: cooldown; template goal: at least params.cooldown_days (14), long enough for a malicious release to be reported and pulled
source: state: .github/dependabot.yml: each updates entry's shortest cooldown days against params.cooldown_days

label: Lockfile packages from the registry
means: Share of installed packages that resolve from the official registry, not another source; higher is better.
goal_source: OpenSSF S2C2F, AUD-2: audit that developers consume OSS through the approved ingestion method; ENF-1: securely configure package source files
source: state: package-lock.json at the root: each package's resolved URL against params.registries, parsed: https, the registry's host, under its path

label: Lockfile packages younger than the cooldown
means: Installed packages, deep ones too, published too recently to trust yet; Dependabot's cooldown covers only direct ones.
goal_source: template goal: no package younger than params.cooldown_days (14), the same wait as security.dependabot_cooldown, applied to every lockfile entry
source: state: package-lock.json against itself params.cooldown_days ago (git); each entry added since on an allowed registry (parsed: https, its host, under its path): a HEAD of its download for Last-Modified, then the registry's full document only where that is recent; no redirects, at most params.max_registry_reads requests; could_not_check on a shallow clone, an unreachable registry or a missing publish time

label: Threat model current with its code
means: Whether the threat model was updated since its code last changed, within the repo's days of grace; on is better.
goal_source: Microsoft SDL practices (read 2026-11-10): practice 3, perform security design review and threat modeling; its threat modeling page: part of your routine development lifecycle; template goal: no change to the covered code since the model's last update
source: state: git log at the root: the latest commit to params.threat_model (a path, or a list of paths that must all exist) against the latest to params.threat_model_covers, less params.threat_model_grace_days; could_not_check on a shallow clone or with no covered paths

label: Credential paths Claude cannot read
means: Share of credential paths, such as .env and keys, that the repo's Claude Code settings deny reading; higher is better.
goal_source: Anthropic, Claude Code settings: permissions.deny with Read(./.env) and Read(./.env.*) keeps secrets out of Claude's reach
source: state: .claude/settings.json permissions.deny Read(...) rules against params.credential_patterns

label: Merged PRs Claude security-reviewed
means: Share of recent merged pull requests where Claude's app or bot left a security review; anyone else's never counts.
goal_source: Anthropic, Claude Code security and GitHub Actions docs: /security-review, or the Claude Code action on a subscription token; template goal: every merge reviewed
source: gh api graphql: the last 20 merged pullRequests (N = 20, as for the Pull requests tab): a head check run from an app in params.review_apps, or a review or comment by a Bot whose login is in params.review_authors, named like params.security_review; only PRs that change a file params.review_paths names, when it names any

label: Latest fixed alert's days open
means: How long the most recently fixed alert stayed open, in days; lower is better.
goal_source: template goal (2026-11-03): an alert is fixed within a week, near 15 days; CISA's BOD 26-04 (June 10, 2026) ranks fixes by risk for federal agencies; its deadlines are in a table this read could not parse (2026-11-10), so the week is the template's own
source: latest: gh api dependabot/alerts, and code-scanning/alerts and secret-scanning/alerts while those features are on: the latest fixed alert, fixed_at or resolved_at (revoked) minus created_at

label: Oldest open alert
means: How long the longest-waiting open alert or finding has been open, in days; lower is better.
goal_source: template goal: no alert waits more than a week, near 15 days; CISA's BOD 26-04 (June 10, 2026) ranks fixes by risk for federal agencies; its deadlines are in a table this read could not parse (2026-11-10), so the week is the template's own
source: state: gh api dependabot/alerts, and code-scanning/alerts, secret-scanning/alerts and code-quality/findings while those features are on: the oldest open one's age at read time

label: Security features billed a month
means: Dollars a month the organization is billed now for GitHub's paid security features; free is the goal.
goal_source: template goal: every security feature at no cost, as GitHub offers code scanning and secret scanning free on a public repo (github.com/security/plans, read 2026-11-03); near is one committer's Secret Protection
source: state: gh api orgs/{owner}/settings/billing/advanced-security, active committers billed for Code Security and Secret Protection, times their list prices ($30 and $19 a month, github.com/security/plans, read 2026-11-03); Code Quality's per-seat licence is not in this read

label: Default branch rules
means: Whether the default branch requires a pull request and blocks force pushes and deletion; on is better.
goal_source: GitHub docs, Available rules for rulesets: Require a pull request before merging, Block force pushes, Restrict deletions
source: state: gh api branches/{branch}/protection and rules/branches/{branch}, {branch} the default branch: a pull request required, force pushes blocked, deletion blocked

label: Required status checks
means: How many automatic checks must pass before a change can join the default branch; more is better.
goal_source: GitHub docs, About protected branches: Require status checks before merging; one required check at least
source: state: gh api branches/{branch}/protection required_status_checks and rules/branches/{branch} required_status_checks, {branch} the default branch

means: Whether GitHub automatically proposes fixes for security holes in our libraries; on is better.
goal_source: GitHub docs, About Dependabot security updates

label: Pages visibility private
means: Whether this page can be seen only by members of the repo's organization; private is better.
